original_question: Are non-trivial stationary nets dense on any closed Riemannian surface?
target_in_paper: Question 11.2.1 (Gromov) in §11.2, "Density of stationary nets and of closed geodesics."
correct_elements: Your draft already identifies the exact open problem the paper states: it has the right objects (non-trivial stationary nets), the right ambient setting (closed Riemannian surfaces), and the right property (density). In fact, it is almost verbatim the formulation of Question 11.2.1.
missing_details: A stationary net must be defined: it is a graph G in a Riemannian surface such that every edge is a geodesic and, at each vertex, the sum of the diverging unit tangent vectors is zero.
The paper imposes that vertices have valence at least 3.
The paper defines non-trivial to mean that the stationary net has at least one vertex of valency at least 3; equivalently, it is not a disjoint union of simple closed geodesics.
The quantifier should be made explicit: the question is for every closed Riemannian surface (S,g).
The meaning of "dense" should be spelled out exactly as the paper does: for every non-empty open subset U of the surface, there should exist such a net intersecting U.
refined_question: Let (S,g) be a closed Riemannian surface. A stationary net is a graph G⊂S such that every edge of G is a geodesic and, at each vertex, the sum of the outgoing unit tangent vectors along the incident edges is zero; all vertices have valence at least 3. Call G non-trivial if it has at least one vertex of valence at least 3, equivalently if it is not a disjoint union of simple closed geodesics. Must non-trivial stationary nets be dense on S, in the sense that for every non-empty open set U⊂S there exists a non-trivial stationary net G with G∩U≠∅?
equivalent_formulation: For each non-empty open subset U of a closed Riemannian surface, is there a stationary net intersecting U?
justification: The draft is targeting exactly the problem recorded in §11.2 as Question 11.2.1 (Gromov). To make it fully stand-alone and faithful to the paper, one must import the immediately preceding definition of a stationary net from §11 and the definition of "nontrivial" from §11.2. The paper itself then restates the density condition using non-empty open subsets, so the refined question stays at exactly the paper's scope and does not broaden to other kinds of geodesic networks or higher-dimensional manifolds.
